CLI walkthroughs use animated command entry with captured output and shorter waits; clone commands are instructional, login uses an example key and the Bitcoin response comes from the recorded local-model session. Transcripts include the source and context of each walkthrough.

Built to do the work

From the working tree
to the Bitcoin stack.

One conversation for code, chain data, RGB assets and configured wallets. Use a built-in command, ask in plain language, or bring your own tools.

01 / BITCOIN

Read the chain. Take action.

Inspect fees, blocks, transactions and addresses. Create a wallet, receive bitcoin and confirm a send from your terminal.

/btc:fees   /btc:tx   /btc:send
02 / LIGHTNING

A closer look at your node.

Decode invoices, inspect channels and check balances. Send and receive with a configured LND node; connect tapd for assets.

/ln:decode   /ln:channels   /ln:pay
03 / LIQUID

Another layer of visibility.

Query Liquid fees, transactions, blocks and asset metadata. Read-only tools for understanding activity on the network.

/liquid:tx   /liquid:asset
04 / RGB

Assets on Bitcoin, by request.

Check balances, create invoices and send RGB assets through an RGB Lightning Node. The node’s changes wait for your approval. Signet test funds only.

--profile rgb   /profile rgb
05 / CASHU

Ecash, from the command line.

Work with mint quotes, tokens and payment requests. Manage your wallet and local mint with the optional Cashu binaries.

/cashu:mint   /cashu:pending
06 / LOCAL

A model that stays on your machine.

Run inference locally with QVAC, Ollama or LM Studio. No API key, and your prompts never reach a cloud provider.

-m qvac/bitcode-local   /models
07 / CODE

Your repository, in context.

Read and edit files, inspect Git changes, run tests and manage processes. Plan the work before making changes.

/repo:review   /plan   /build
08 / EXTENSIONS

Make room for your workflow.

Connect MCP tools, resources and prompts. Load local skills, add Markdown commands and delegate bounded tasks to subagents.

/mcp   /skills   /subagent

Capabilities depend on your configuration. RGB needs a running RGB Lightning Node and kaleido-mcp; Wavelength read-only tools need its optional binaries.

Meet the Sats

Four agents.
One bitcode.

Pick a Sat for the job. Each one has its own role, its own tools and limits enforced in code, in the CLI and in the desktop app.

Preview

SAT / 01

Node

Bitcoin infrastructure

Reads Bitcoin, Lightning, Liquid and Taproot Assets data. Keeps the networks apart and never sends funds.

  • read files
  • network
  • no shell
  • no wallet

SAT / 02

Script

Code and implementation

Inspects before changing code, implements the requested scope and verifies the result. Commands wait for your approval.

  • write files
  • shell on approval
  • no network
  • no wallet

SAT / 03

Hash

Verification and security

Reviews changes, evidence and security boundaries. Separates verified findings from assumptions.

  • read files
  • no shell
  • no network
  • no wallet

SAT / 04

Merkle

Orchestration

Plans the work and delegates to Node, Script and Hash, one level deep. Delegating never hands over permissions.

  • read files
  • delegate
  • no shell
  • no wallet

Choose a Sat.

The choice applies to your next messages and is saved with the session. /reset returns to bitcode.

/sats
/sat merkle
/sat info hash

Watch them work.

Open the local companion: an animated view of each Sat's state and of Merkle's delegations. Interactive mode only.

node bitcode.mjs --sats

Sat permissions are application limits, not an operating-system sandbox. In the CLI, a shell command you approve runs with your user's rights. In the desktop app, the agent worker runs isolated with bubblewrap.

Use the exact ID offered by your deployment

Interactive

node bitcode.mjs

Talk through a task. Mention files with @path and inspect available commands with /help.

Scriptable

node bitcode.mjs --read-only \
  --json -p "review this repo"

Get an answer, tool events and usage as JSON. Use read-only mode for repository reviews.

Ollama

node bitcode.mjs \
  -m ollama/qwen3.8:27b

Use your running Ollama instance with a matching downloaded model tag. Network tools still contact their services.

QVAC

npm --prefix integrations/qvac start
node bitcode.mjs -m qvac/bitcode-local

Start the local QVAC server, then pick its configured aliases with /models. Weights download on first use.

bitcode Desktop

bitcode on your desktop.
Starting with Linux.

The same agent and the same Sats, in a workspace with projects, an editor, Git and a terminal. It is still in development, with no installable release yet.

In development

Development preview on Linux. The interface and features may change.

Projects and sessions.

Open a folder and keep several chats for each project. Sessions are shared with the CLI.

Editor, Git and terminal.

An editor that warns about changes on disk, Git diff, stage and commit, and your own terminal.

The Sats, in the chat.

Choose bitcode or a Sat for each chat and a model for each Sat. Approval cards appear in the conversation.

An isolated agent.

The agent worker runs in a bubblewrap sandbox, without your home folder or direct network access, and never receives provider keys.

You approve the actions.

One-time approvals tied to the session, a local-only mode, and your consent before a local model hands off to a cloud provider.

Bitcoin and RGB wallets.

A Bitcoin test wallet and RGB wallet sessions, with an RGB node panel read through Tether WDK. Every send waits for your payment approval.

Every network, read-only.

Lightning, Taproot Assets, Liquid and Cashu in view, each environment verified from its genesis block or the node’s API.

Made for the desktop.

Tray icon, notifications without sensitive content, light and dark themes, English and Italian.

Not in the preview yet.

Test operations for Lightning, Taproot Assets, Liquid and Cashu, a Liquid wallet, an OS-level network gateway for commands, attaching from the CLI, checkpoints, updates and a tested .deb package.

Installation guide ↗Provider setup ↗
SourceOllamaQVACScriptable
Terminal / Bash
# Get the source
git clone https://github.com/faktotum-project/bitcode.git
cd bitcode

# Install without optional wallet builds
npm ci --ignore-scripts

# Check your setup and configure a provider
node bitcode.mjs doctor
node bitcode.mjs login openai
node bitcode.mjs -m openai/gpt-6-astra

Inside the agent

Use /login to configure another provider, /setting to inspect your setup, and /help to explore commands. Ollama uses a running local model and needs no API key.

Ollama
node bitcode.mjs -m ollama/gpt-oss:20b

Start Ollama and download a model first. Replace the tag with one installed on your machine. Network tools still contact their services.

QVAC
npm --prefix integrations/qvac start
node bitcode.mjs -m qvac/bitcode-local

Start the QVAC integration after source installation. Weights download on first use. See the QVAC setup guide.

Scriptable
node bitcode.mjs --read-only --json -p "review this repo"

After source installation, configure a provider or select a local model. Read-only mode returns JSON without changing your repository.

Cashu and Wavelength need optional binaries. Run doctor to see what is available, and follow the setup instructions for the tools you need.
